spec.credit: UPSC CSE (Main) 2024 · Economics optional Paper I · Q4(a)
spec.text: Describe the mechanism of credit creation by commercial banks and its implications on multiplier effect. Analyse some of the limitations that can jeopardise the implications on multiplier effect.

scenes.vo: UPSC, twenty twenty-four. Economics optional, twenty marks. You know this topic: the CRR, the SLR, the multiplier. So why does this answer still miss the question? Let's fix it, line by line.

spec.text: Describe the mechanism of credit creation by commercial banks and its implications on multiplier effect. Analyse some of the limitations that can jeopardise the implications on multiplier effect.

demands.label: What it does to the multiplier

scenes.vo: Read it slowly. Describe means set out how it works. Analyse means split it into parts, and show the links. So there are three jobs: the mechanism, what it does to the multiplier, and the limits that can break it.

spec.stamp: ILLUSTRATIVE · WRITTEN BY US, NOT A CANDIDATE'S COPY

items.text: Banking is very important for the economy of any country.
Commercial banks create credit by lending out the deposits they receive from the public. This process is called credit creation.
Multiplier = 1/CRR. RBI's CRR is 3%, so the multiplier is about 33. So ₹100 of deposits becomes about ₹3,300 in the economy.
Limitations: banks must keep CRR and SLR, so they cannot lend all their deposits. RBI also changes the repo rate.
Limits: what can break the multiplier
• Cash drain: people keep cash, so a higher _cash-deposit ratio_ cuts m. India: m 5.57 → 5.20 as cdr rose 0.16 → 0.18 (RBI Bulletin, 2022).
• Spare reserves: banks may not lend. US, 1930–1933: money fell about 35% while the base rose about 20% (IGNOU).
• Loan demand: the rounds go on only if people borrow (IGNOU).
Conclusion: banks play a very important role in the economy.
So the multiplier is a _ceiling, not a constant_: cash, spare reserves and weak loan demand keep real money below it.

scenes.vo: Start with the limits, because that is where this answer loses the question. It says banks must keep the CRR and the SLR, and that RBI changes the repo rate. But the CRR is already inside the multiplier: one over the reserve ratio. It sets how big the multiplier is. The question asks something else: what stops real money from reaching that size? This is not a knowledge problem. It is a reading problem.

scenes.vo: There are two more problems, and they are different. Banks do not just lend out deposits: when a bank lends, it opens a new deposit. And one over the CRR ignores the cash that people keep. These are concept gaps. A better structure will not fix them.

lines.text: A loan opens a new deposit · NCERT Class XII, 3.3
Cash held shrinks the multiplier · IGNOU Unit 13
Our film: how banks create money

scenes.vo: Learn those first. A loan opens a new deposit. Cash that people hold shrinks the multiplier. Our film on how banks create money shows both, and we will come back to them.

scenes.vo: Then the limits. Strike them out. A limit must say what breaks, and how. Cash drain: people keep cash, so the cash ratio rises and the multiplier falls. India's fell from five point five seven to five point two zero, as the cash ratio rose.
